# Engine gap: retire the legacy `act` / `clockCost` CSV columns

## Problem statement

The Gym's *Long Erasure* content file still declares `act` and `clockCost` as
CSV columns, and the spike's Phaser-free rule module reads them, even though the
episode beat-sheet manifest is now the authoritative home for act membership
(`act.scenes[].id`) and pacing (`beat.clockCost`). Until the columns retire, a
writer can still author beat-sheet data in the wrong place, and the same value
lives in two files that must be kept in sync by hand.

## Users

- **As a content writer**, I want an `act`/`clockCost` cell to be refused as an
  unknown column, so I cannot accidentally put beat-sheet data in the CSV.
- **As the spike's maintainer**, I want `GymLongErasureGame` to read act and
  pacing from the episode manifest, so the demo exercises the same source of
  truth as the episode runner.
- **As an engine maintainer**, I want one authoritative home for act membership
  and pacing, so the content file and the manifest cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `LONG_ERASURE_CONTENT_ADAPTER` no longer declares `act` or `clockCost` in
  `columns`, `editableColumns` or `newCardDefaults`; `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER` (the
  default demo content) is unchanged.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv` and every test fixture that
  declares the two columns are migrated: the headers and cells are gone, and
  every card's act membership and clock cost resolve from
  `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json`.
- `GymLongErasureGame` derives each card's `act` and `clockCost` from the
  episode manifest (the same manifest the scene already imports for
  `resources.bounds`); a card absent from the manifest is a loud
  `invalid-content` error, never an inferred default.
- The retired columns are refused by the authoring/tooling path: a
  `storylines:author --field act=…` or `--field clockCost=…` write fails with
  `unknown content column`, and the regenerated artefacts
  (`long-erasure-manifest.json`, `long-erasure-graph.mmd`) no longer embed
  `fields.act` / `fields.clockCost`, so `npm run storylines:graph -- --check`
  is clean.
- The migration-only `clock-cost-mismatch` rule is left as a documented,
  permanently-green no-op (its no-column test stays green), with the removal
  decision and rationale recorded in its module docs; it is not extended into a
  general legacy-column mechanism.
- At least one unit test proves the retired columns are refused and that a CSV
  without them loads; the changed-scope unit profile is green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, the GDD G10 disposition, and any relevant README or docs-site
  entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A writer on the GDD game can no longer author `act`/`clockCost` in the CSV —
act membership and pacing now live only in the episode manifest, so the beat
sheet has one source of truth and cannot drift from the spike.

## Constraints

- No new machinery: this is a content-format change plus a migration, not a new
  subsystem. Do not build a general "legacy column" framework around one rule.
- The spike's public behaviour (pressure clock, act gating/completion, journey
  score) must be unchanged; only its data source moves.
- The Gym demo content (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`) must stay
  byte-identical.
- CHANGELOG is out of scope (release pipeline owns it); no CI/CD pipeline tests.
- Pushes go to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Existing state

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` declares `act` and `clockCost` in the
  Long Erasure adapter's `columns` and `editableColumns`, with defaults `I` /
  `1`, and documents them as the migration-only columns G10 retires.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` exports `LEGACY_CLOCK_COST_COLUMN` and
  documents the column as migration-only, naming this item (G10) as the
  removal trigger.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` reads
  `card.fields.act` / `card.fields.clockCost` via `parseAct` /
  `parseClockCost` for `LongErasureCard.act` and `.clockCost`.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` already imports
  `long-erasure-episode.json` and passes `resources.bounds` to the content
  loader, so the manifest is available at content-load time.
- The episode manifest already carries the same data: all 19 CSV cards are
  assigned (15 beats + 4 endings), act membership is derivable from
  `acts[].scenes[].beats[]`, and every `beat.clockCost` currently agrees with
  its CSV cell — so no value needs re-authoring, only a source change.
- `clock-cost-mismatch` is delivered (CG-0MWSJYS20005CBQ5) and already a no-op
  when the adapter declares no `clockCost` column.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-manifest.json` (graph) and
  `long-erasure-graph.mmd` are generated from the CSV and currently embed
  `fields.act` / `fields.clockCost`.

## Desired change

1. Drop `act` and `clockCost` from the Long Erasure adapter's `columns`,
   `editableColumns` and `newCardDefaults`, and update its doc comment.
2. Migrate `long-erasure.csv` and every fixture that declares the columns;
   regenerate the graph manifest + Mermaid artefacts.
3. Teach `GymLongErasureGame` to derive `act` / `clockCost` from the episode
   manifest (via the scene's existing import), with a loud error for an
   unassigned card.
4. Keep `clock-cost-mismatch` as a documented no-op (or record the decision to
   remove it) and confirm the authoring path refuses the retired columns.
5. Update tests and the GDD G10 disposition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — remove the two columns, the
  `editableColumns` entries and the defaults; update the adapter doc comment.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — retire/retain `LEGACY_CLOCK_COST_COLUMN`
  and its migration docs (decision recorded in this item).
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv` — drop the `act` / `clockCost`
  headers and cells.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` — derive `act` / `clockCost` from
  the manifest; remove `parseAct` / `parseClockCost` CSV reads.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` — pass the manifest act/beat
  data into content loading.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-manifest.json` —
  regenerate without the retired fields.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-graph.mmd` — regenerate.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — keep `clock-cost-mismatch` as a
  documented no-op (or remove the unreachable predicate) and update docs.
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/**` — migrate fixtures that declare the columns
  (`clock-cost-drift.csv`, `gdd-resource-trades.csv`, `irreversible-grant.csv`,
  `prose/long-erasure-*.csv`, and any scene-guard fixture that carries them).
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`,
  `tests/gym/LongErasureContent.test.ts`,
  `tests/story-line/content/episode-manifest-clock-cost.test.ts` — update/add
  coverage.
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — update the G10 disposition/status.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWR0BFMW003856N` — Engine gap: episode manifest schema and validator
  (storylines:manifest) — **completed**; delivered the manifest validator this
  item's migration check depends on.
- `CG-0MWSJYS20005CBQ5` — Episode manifest legacy clock-cost migration rule —
  **completed**; delivered `clock-cost-mismatch`, which this item leaves as a
  no-op / retires.
- `CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ` — Engine gap: episode beat-sheet and objective layer
  (createEpisodeRunner) — **completed**; the runner that reads `beat.clockCost`
  as the authoritative pacing source.
- `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` — GDD: full story-line game (Approach C — scene beat
  sheet) informed by the Gym spike — **completed**; the GDD this gap came from.
- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — GDD engine-gap backlog — **completed**; entry G10.
- GDD §2.1 (composition contract), §2.4 (`clock-cost-mismatch`),
  §2.9 ("the two retired columns"), §6 (G10).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Routine questions answered by repo search (no producer decision required):

- **Q: Does the episode manifest already carry the values, so no re-authoring is
  needed?** — Answer (agent research): Yes. All 19 CSV cards are assigned
  (15 beats + 4 endings) and every `beat.clockCost` agrees with its CSV cell;
  act membership is derivable from `acts[].scenes[].beats[]`. Source:
  `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json`,
  `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv`.
- **Q: How does the spike get the manifest today?** — Answer (agent research):
  `GymLongErasureScene` already imports `long-erasure-episode.json` and passes
  `resources.bounds` into `longErasureContentFromCsv`; the act/beat data can ride
  the same path. Source: `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts:87,186–190`.
- **Q: Should `clock-cost-mismatch` be deleted once the column retires?** —
  Answer (agent decision/documented assumption): keep it as a documented
  no-op — its own delivered AC says retiring the column removes the check
  "without a code change", and the migration item warns against building a
  general legacy-column mechanism. Source: `CG-0MWSJYS20005CBQ5` ACs and risks.
- **Q: Does the authoring path already refuse an undeclared column?** — Answer
  (agent research): Yes. `storylines:author --field <name>` rejects a column the
  file header lacks with `unknown content column`; dropping the adapter entries
  is what makes `act`/`clockCost` unknown. Source:
  `src/story-line/content/mutate.ts:280–286`.
- **Q: Is the item now unblocked?** — Answer (agent research): Yes. The GDD
  epic and G2 (manifest validator) are both `completed`, and the item's
  `startOn` scheduling hold was cleared. Source: `wl dep list`, work-item
  comments.

## Assumptions

- The episode manifest is the single authoritative beat sheet; the spike may
  consume it without a new loader abstraction.
- The `long-erasure-manifest.json` graph artefact and `long-erasure-graph.mmd`
  are regenerable with `npm run storylines:graph` (checked with `--check`).
- Keeping `clock-cost-mismatch` as a permanent no-op is acceptable; if the
  producer prefers deleting the unreachable predicate and
  `LEGACY_CLOCK_COST_COLUMN`, that is a small, contained follow-up.

## Risks

- **Scope creep:** touching fixtures may reveal unrelated drift; that is a new
  work item, not extra scope here.
- **Silent fixture loss:** a fixture that relied on the columns to exercise
  `clock-cost-mismatch` must keep a dedicated copy if that rule's test is to
  remain meaningful — verify before deleting.
- **Artefact drift:** forgetting to regenerate the graph manifest/Mermaid makes
  `storylines:graph -- --check` fail; the check is the guard.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MWNHZ8NM002ZJMI** – Long Erasure CSV content + structural tests (completed)
- **CG-0MWNHZA1A007BRVT** – Long Erasure Phaser-free narrative module (completed)
- **CG-0MWUQUJ84005L4MF** – Gym long-erasure: declare hull irreversible + fixture rows + tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — matched: 0mwnfvlyt003m7xf, 0mwpy2ece002p2nh, 0mwr0bat30015dpq, 0mwr0bfmw003856n, absent (+316 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, abstraction, acceptable, acceptance, act (+309 more)
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, act, acts, adapter (+282 more)

# Engine gap: keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order

## Problem statement

The story-line presentation contract promises a full keyboard path — choose an
option with `1`–`6` or arrows + Enter, traverse focus inside an open overlay and
activate with Enter/Space, and close only the topmost modal with Escape — but the
engine exports no helper for any of it, so every game must hand-roll `keydown`
listeners. Today only the panels' own toggle keys are bound, which makes
[GDD §3.4.4](docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md#344-keyboard-and-touch-input-paths)
aspirational and leaves §3.8 unable to claim the keyboard path is testable.

## Users

- **Keyboard-only / switch-access player** — plays the whole story-line run without
  a pointer: `1`–`6` (or arrows + Enter) picks a choice, Tab/Shift+Tab walks an
  open overlay's controls, Enter/Space activates, Escape dismisses only the
  modal on top.
  - *As a keyboard-only player, I can select a choice with a digit key so I never
    have to locate option rows with a mouse.*
  - *As a keyboard-only player, I can reach and activate every control in an open
    journal/confirmation overlay with Tab and Enter, and Escape closes only that
    overlay.*
- **Game developer (story-line build epic, Gym maintainer)** — attaches two shared
  helpers and inherits the keyboard contract plus its tests instead of
  re-implementing listeners per scene.
  - *As a developer, I call `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, …)` once per scene and
    get digits, arrow wrap, Enter/Space activation and a disposer, so the keyboard
    path cannot drift between games.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ui` exports two additive helpers from the `@ui` barrel — `attachChoiceNavigation(scene, { count, onChoose, onHighlight?, keys? })` and `attachOverlayFocus(scene, focusables, { onEscape, onFocusChange? })` — each returning an idempotent disposer, with no change to existing `Overlay`/`OverlayManager`/`OverlayButton` signatures required by callers.
- Choice navigation maps in-range digit keys (`1`–`9`) to option indices, moves the highlight with ArrowUp/ArrowDown plus ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (wrapping at both ends), activates the highlighted option with Enter/Space via `onChoose(index)`, reports the highlighted index through `onHighlight(index)`, and is completely inert while a managed overlay is open or after disposal.
- Overlay focus traverses the supplied focusables in list order (Tab forward, Shift+Tab backward, wrapping), activates the focused item with Enter/Space via that item's `onActivate`, reports focus changes through `onFocusChange(index)` so the game can render a visible focus state, and closes only the topmost managed overlay on Escape — never a lower modal, never the game, and it leaves Escape unhandled when no managed overlay is open (so `SettingsPanel`'s default `Escape` toggle keeps working, per GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- Both helpers install and remove their `keydown`/scene-`shutdown` listeners through an injectable keyboard seam so they are unit-testable headless (same seam pattern as `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts`), never throw when the scene has no keyboard plugin, and leave no listener behind after disposal or scene shutdown.
- Headless unit tests cover digit selection (including out-of-range), arrow wrap in both directions, Enter/Space activation, focus traversal and wrap, Escape closing the topmost overlay only, inertness while a modal is open, and disposer/shutdown teardown; one browser test proves the real `scene.input.keyboard` wiring and the rendered focus state on a parented overlay.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the new helper section and, if the module qualifies, the node-safe surface manifest), and the GDD status rows that currently read "Gap B7" (§3.4.4, §3.6 B7, §3.8 and §6 G11), plus the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A keyboard-only player can play a story-line run end to end — pick choices by
number or arrow, walk an overlay's controls, and dismiss only the modal on top —
instead of being forced back to the pointer.

## Constraints

- **Small effort band** (0.5–2 days, GDD G11): one new `src/ui` module plus tests
  and doc flips. No new dependency, no refactor of the overlay primitives.
- **Headless-testable by construction.** Keyboard access must go through an
  injected seam (`{ on, off }`-shaped) rather than a direct `scene.input` reach,
  matching `narration-reveal.ts`'s `bindInput` pattern; the module should stay
  Phaser-type-only so it can join the node-safe `src/ui` manifest.
- **No key-binding collisions.** `HelpPanel` (`?`) and `SettingsPanel` (Escape)
  keep their own listeners; the new Escape handler must be stack-aware, not a
  second global listener that fights them (GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- **No bespoke overlay work.** Focusables are game-owned objects parented into
  `hudContainer`; the helper wires keys and reports focus, it does not build
  overlays. `OverlayDialogHandle.close()` remains the close path.
- **Accessibility floor preserved.** A visible focus indication is mandatory: the
  helper must make the focused item visually distinct (via `onFocusChange` plus a
  default style hook), and there must be no motion dependency (reduced motion is a
  no-op because nothing animates).
- **Out of scope (record as linked follow-ups, not scope creep):** screen-reader
  live-region announcements, DOM (`tabindex`) focus management for DOM-rendered
  debug tools, arrow-key navigation of the market/card rows, and a Gym demo scene
  (the GDD requires the helper, not a new Gym scene).

## Risks and mitigations

- **Key-stealing risk** — a global `keydown` listener that swallows digits or
  Enter could break a scene's own bindings. *Mitigation:* the helpers consume
  only the keys they own, expose `isBlocked()`, and are inert without a
  registered focus/choice context; a test pins "no binding when disposed".
- **Escape double-handling risk** — `SettingsPanel` already defaults to Escape.
  *Mitigation:* stack-aware handling plus the "unhandled when no managed overlay
  is open" test (GDD §3.2 rule 3).
- **Accessibility theatre risk** — navigation that works but has no visible focus
  is unusable. *Mitigation:* mandatory `onFocusChange`/`setFocusVisual` contract
  and a browser test that asserts the rendered focus state.
- **Listener-leak risk** — early returns on scene shutdown can leave listeners.
  *Mitigation:* one disposer path used by the disposer, the `shutdown` hook and
  the error path; a test asserts every `on` has a matching `off`.
- **Scope-creep risk** — screen-reader live regions, DOM `tabindex` focus for
  debug tools, market/card arrow navigation and a Gym demo are attractive but
  out of scope; they are recorded as linked follow-ups rather than folded in.
- **Assumption:** the GDD's wording ("`1`–`6`, or arrows + Enter") is the whole
  contract; any additional keybinding scheme requires a producer decision before
  implementation.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/index.ts` exports the overlay primitives (`createOverlayBackground`,
  `createOverlayDialog`, `dismissOverlay`, `OverlayManager`,
  `ParameterizedOverlay`) but no keyboard helper.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` registers its own `keydown` listener in
  `setupKeyboardShortcut()` and removes it in `destroy()`; `SettingsPanel.ts`
  does the same for `Escape`/end-turn capture; `SettingsStore.ts` exposes
  `getEndTurnKeybind()`/`setEndTurnKeybind('Enter')` for one game action only.
- `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` already enforces one live overlay (`showOverlay()`
  dismisses the previous one) but tracks objects, not a modal stack, and binds no
  keys. `src/ui/Overlay.ts` exposes `OverlayDialogHandle.close()`.
- `src/ui/ParameterizedOverlay.ts` and `src/ui/OverlayButton.ts` are
  pointer-only (`pointerover`/`pointerout`/`pointerdown`), so their buttons are
  currently unreachable by keyboard.
- `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts` is the established headless pattern: it binds
  `scene.input.keyboard` defensively through `bindInput(...)` and skips a
  destructor-less input object.
- Precedent for a keyboard picker exists only as a **game-local DOM overlay**
  (`../tce-main-street/src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts`, arrows + Enter +
  Escape on a DOM input); it is not reusable from the engine and does not cover
  Phaser overlay objects.
- Nothing in `src/ui` reads `'Tab'`, `'Enter'` or digit keys today (verified by
  grep), so the new bindings introduce no regression to existing scenes.

## Desired change

Add one additive keyboard module (working name `src/ui/keyboard-navigation.ts`)
with a pure, injectable core:

```ts
export interface KeyboardSeam {
  on(event: 'keydown', handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void): void;
  off(event: 'keydown', handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void): void;
}

export interface ChoiceNavigationOptions {
  count: number;                       // visible options
  onChoose(index: number): void;       // Enter/Space or digit activation
  onHighlight?(index: number): void;   // arrows / digits moved the highlight
  keys?: { digits?: boolean; arrows?: boolean; activate?: boolean };
  keyboard?: KeyboardSeam;             // defaults to scene.input.keyboard
  isBlocked?(): boolean;               // e.g. true while a modal is open
}

export interface OverlayFocusable {
  onActivate(): void;
  setFocusVisual?(focused: boolean): void;  // game-owned visual
}

export interface OverlayFocusOptions {
  onEscape(): void;                    // pop the topmost managed overlay
  onFocusChange?(index: number): void;
  keyboard?: KeyboardSeam;
}

export function attachChoiceNavigation(
  scene: Phaser.Scene | null | undefined,
  options: ChoiceNavigationOptions,
): () => void;

export function attachOverlayFocus(
  scene: Phaser.Scene | null | undefined,
  focusables: OverlayFocusable[],
  options: OverlayFocusOptions,
): () => void;
```

Semantics: digit keys select (and activate, or highlight+activate — decided in
plan against the GDD wording) indices `0..count-1`; arrows move the highlight
with wrap; Enter/Space activates; Tab/Shift+Tab walk the overlay focus list with
wrap; Escape pops only the topmost managed overlay. Helpers no-op safely with a
null/headless scene, are inert while blocked, and dispose every listener on the
returned disposer and on scene `shutdown`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/keyboard-navigation.ts` — new module: seam types, pure index/traversal
  reducers, `attachChoiceNavigation`, `attachOverlayFocus`, disposer plumbing.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — barrel exports for the two helpers and their option types.
- `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` — add the module if the surface check proves it
  Phaser-value-free (Phaser is type-only).
- `src/ui/OverlayManager.ts` — optional additive managed-modal stack (or the new
  module owns its own stack; the plan picks one, with no caller breakage).
- `tests/ui/keyboard-navigation.test.ts` — new headless unit suite (injected seam).
- `tests/ui/keyboard-navigation.browser.test.ts` — new browser suite proving real
  `scene.input.keyboard` wiring and the focus visual on a parented overlay.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — helper reference section (hotkeys, focus order, Escape
  stack, reduced-motion no-op, headless seam).
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — §3.4.4 status rows, §3.6 B7, §3.8
  "keyboard path is untestable", §6 G11 disposition.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — GDD engine-gap backlog (source of G11).
- `CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ` — the build epic that consumes this capability.
- `CG-0MWR0BJBU005TDTT` — sibling engine gap G9 (act/scene transition
  presentation); same presentation-contract family.
- `CG-0MWR0BL4Q000OYG6` — sibling engine gap G12 (shared verbosity preference).
- `CG-0MWPY2CHF003AHE1` — GDD presentation contract (UI, audio, accessibility)
  that defines §3.4.4 and the B7 gap.
- `CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5` / `CG-0MTIR0HK4005SEQW` — completed Market Card Cheat
  tool: game-local keyboard picker precedent (arrows + Enter + Escape), not a
  shared helper.
- `CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN` — node-safe `@ui` surface manifest and check (constrains
  how the new module must be importable).

### Duplicate-check outcome

Performed (`wl search` over "keyboard focus overlay", "accessibility", "choice
list"). No completed item satisfies this item's ACs: the only keyboard-navigation
work is the Market Card Cheat/Tool pair, which is a **game-local dev tool**
DOM overlay, not a shared `@ui` helper, and does not cover focus order or
topmost-only Escape. Partial-overlap note recorded in
[Related work](#related-work).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

All questions below were resolved from repository evidence or a documented
reasonable assumption (the shared interview contract's **routine** class); none
required a producer decision, so the item was not held for producer review.

- **Q: Is the scope exactly GDD G11 (choice navigation + overlay focus), or does
  B7 also require keyboard activation of narrative/journal page controls?**
  — Answer (routine, documented assumption): page controls are implemented as
  focusable overlay items, so `attachOverlayFocus` makes them Tab-reachable and
  Enter/Space-activatable with no extra API. Evidence:
  [GDD §3.4.4](docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md#344-keyboard-and-touch-input-paths)
  lists paging under the same B7 row and §3.2 requires journal page buttons as
  the non-wheel path. No separate paging helper is in scope.
- **Q: Which keys move the highlight — arrows only, or also `1`–`6`?**
  — Answer (routine, documented assumption): both, per the GDD (`1`–`6`, or
  arrows + Enter). Digits are out-of-range safe (indices beyond `count` are
  ignored) and arrows wrap.
- **Q: Does Escape in the new helper collide with `SettingsPanel`'s default
  Escape toggle?** — Answer (routine, documented assumption): no, because the
  helper only consumes Escape when a managed overlay is open and GDD §3.2 rule 3
  already forbids opening an engine panel and a managed modal simultaneously; a
  test will pin "Escape with no managed overlay is unhandled".
- **Q: Should the helpers render a focus highlight themselves?** — Answer
  (routine, documented assumption): no artwork ships; the helper reports
  `onFocusChange(index)` and calls an optional `setFocusVisual(focused)` so the
  game keeps ownership of its option rows. A visible focus state is still an AC,
  proven by the browser test.
- **Q: Does this need a Gym scene?** — Answer (routine, documented assumption):
  no. The GDD requires the engine capability (and its tests), and G11's effort
  band is `S`; a Gym demo would push it to `M` and is recorded as out of scope.
- **Q: Does the module belong in the node-safe `@ui` manifest?** — Answer
  (routine, to be proven by the build gate): yes if
  `npm run check:ui-node-surface` passes with Phaser as a type-only import;
  otherwise the module stays out of the manifest (never edit the module to fit
  the list).
- **Q: Issue type and priority?** — Answer (routine): `task` / `low`, as filed
  by the GDD backlog; no new priority signal found.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM3B3CBI1GF6UCE** – Implement Resolved-Inputs Helper (completed)
- **CG-0MLSGNPFI0ZX35FR** – Directory Structure and Placeholder Modules (completed)
- **CG-0MM3B31S50OYMC59** – Define Setup Types in Core Engine (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — matched: 0mwpy2ece002p2nh, accessibility, action, activation, add (+109 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: accessibility, action, activation, add, arrow (+96 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: accessibility, action, add, behaviour, bind (+82 more)

## Summary

Fourth vertical slice: adopt `ResourceHud` in `GymLongErasureScene` at the `statusBar.resources` SLL anchor, replacing the bespoke `resourcesText` / `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel` status path while keeping the scene's observable behaviour green.

## Target outcome

The in-repo five-key economy renders through the shared component — declared keys, labels, bounds and the irreversible subset from the committed manifest — and the Gym browser suite still proves the same starting resources, per-choice changes and layout anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GymLongErasureScene` renders its `statusBar.resources` surface through the new component (declared keys, display labels, irreversible set and bounds from the committed `long-erasure-episode.json`; values from the resource projection's `getResources`) instead of the bespoke `resourcesLine` / `resourceLabel`, and keeps its existing observable behaviour (starting resources, per-choice resource changes, layout anchor) green in the browser suite.
- The component is constructed at the SLL-resolved `statusBar.resources` anchor with right alignment; no literal coordinate is introduced, and the bespoke status renderer (`resourcesText`, `resourcesLine`, `resourceLabel`) is removed.
- The epilogue's "Left when the timeline closed" summary reuses the same derived labels map (it does not re-implement the HUD), and the scene passes `bounds` / `irreversible` from `LONG_ERASURE_EPISODE_MANIFEST` rather than a copied literal.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` stays green; assertions are extended only where needed to observe the component's rendered text/markers. Scene help-text and Gym-index documentation changes are handed to the documentation slice (`CG-0MWZ9WD9P003IAQM`) rather than duplicated here.

## Minimal implementation

1. Construct `ResourceHud` in `buildChrome()` at the resolved `statusBar.resources` point with `declaredKeys` from the content, `labels` from a derived label map, `bounds` / `irreversible` from the manifest, and the run's resource bag.
2. Call `setResources` from `render()`; delete `resourcesText`, `resourcesLine` and `resourceLabel`.
3. Keep the epilogue line by formatting it from the same labels map.
4. Run the Gym browser suite; extend the HUD assertions only if the rendered text/markers need direct observation.

## Key Files

- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts`
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts`
- `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`

## Dependencies

- Child 2 (bounds/irreversible markers).
- Child 3 (update path).

## Deliverables

- Gym Long Erasure HUD rendered by the shared component at the SLL anchor.
- Bespoke status-line helpers removed; browser suite green with the adopted component.


## Impact

A Long Erasure player sees the five-key economy rendered by the shared ResourceHud — with its bounds, edge-state words and the irreversible hull marked — so the economy readout is consistent with every other game that adopts the component, and a resource change after a choice is animated in place.

# Presentation helper: presentSceneExit()

**Summary:** The Phaser-based `presentSceneExit()` function that renders an act/scene banner from `{ actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route }`, positions every element from injected SLL anchors (a `sceneBanner` zone), sequences the steps (title → outcome → route), and returns a promise that resolves on dismissal.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Renders text objects for `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, and `route` — each positioned from the provided SLL `resolveAnchor` callback, never absolute pixel coordinates.
2. Sequences steps in order: act/scene title → outcome → route — with configurable dwell times (`stepMs`).
3. The outcome displays the word (`success` / `partial` / `failure`) as primary text, with optional colour tint as secondary cue only.
4. Dismisses on click/key press (`skipOnInput`), showing all text instantly without further animation.
5. Auto-advances after `autoAdvanceMs` (default configurable, default 3000ms).
6. Returns a `SceneExitPresentationHandle` with `{ skip(), destroy(), promise, readonly plan, readonly done, readonly destroyed }`.
7. Does not move the camera — a documented note says `runSceneTransition` (or the game) owns the camera fade/slide.
8. **Covers parent AC 0.** A new shared helper `presentSceneExit()` in `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts` (exported from the `@ui` barrel) renders an act/scene banner from `{ actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route }`, positions **every** element from injected SLL anchors (a `sceneBanner` zone: `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, `route`) — never an absolute pixel coordinate — and returns a promise that resolves once when the banner is dismissed.
9. **Covers parent AC 2.** The outcome is colour-independent: the banner prints the outcome word (`success` / `partial` / `failure`) as its primary channel, with tint only as a secondary cue; a test asserts the word is present in each outcome state.
10. **Covers parent AC 6.** The presentation can be layered on the existing camera transition without either double-playing motion: the helper does not itself move the camera, and a documented note says `runSceneTransition` (or the game) owns the camera fade/slide.

## Minimal Implementation
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`: `presentSceneExit()` + `SceneExitPresentationHandle` type.
- SFX played via injected `SoundManager` with key from `resolveSceneExitSfxKey()`.
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`: Phaser browser test asserting banner renders, sequences steps, dismisses on input.

## Deliverables
- Working code, tests and docs for this slice, committed and green.

## Dependencies
- CG-0MWZCKY1W008JV83
- CG-0MWZCLIBF000SU2U

## Key Files
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`

# Reduced-motion instant presentation

**Summary:** When reduced motion is enabled (either via the explicit `reducedMotion: true` flag or `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`), `presentSceneExit()` presents all information synchronously in one step — no tween, no timer, no SFX — and still resolves the promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. With reduced motion, the banner renders all four fields (act title, scene title, outcome word, route) immediately in one step.
2. No tween, timer or SFX is created when reduced motion is active.
3. The promise resolves on the single instant step (same as normal dismissal).
4. The browser test asserts the instant state contains all four fields.
5. Reduced motion suppresses SFX in addition to motion (per `docs/ui-animations.md` → Accessibility).
6. **Covers parent AC 3.** Reduced motion (explicit `reducedMotion` flag or `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`) presents the same information synchronously in one step — no tween, no timer, no SFX — and still resolves the promise; a test asserts the instant state contains the act title, scene title, outcome word and route.

## Minimal Implementation
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`: reduced-motion branch in `presentSceneExit()` — render merged instant step, skip scheduling.
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`: browser test for reduced-motion instant path.

## Deliverables

# Idempotent teardown and lifecycle

**Summary:** `presentSceneExit()` teardown must be total and idempotent: `destroy()` (and scene `shutdown`) removes the timer, tween, every input listener, and every created game object — leaving no orphans and allowing re-invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `destroy()` removes all timers, tweens, input listeners and game objects created by the helper.
2. Calling `destroy()` multiple times is idempotent — no errors, no double-cleanup side effects.
3. Calling `skip()` after `destroy()` is a no-op (does not throw).
4. The handle exposes `readonly destroyed: boolean` reflecting lifecycle state.
5. After `destroy()`, the promise has resolved and the `done` flag is `true`.
6. Browser test asserts no orphaned game objects remain in the scene after teardown.
7. **Covers parent AC 5.** Dismissal and teardown are total and idempotent: a click/key skips to the end (full information, no further tween), an auto-advance dismisses after a configurable dwell (`autoAdvanceMs`), and `destroy()`/scene `shutdown` removes the timer, tween, every input listener and every created game object, leaving no orphans; tests assert idempotence and no residue.

## Minimal Implementation
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`: `destroy()` implementation with cleanup list (objects array, timer, listener refs).
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`: teardown assertions.

## Deliverables
- Working code, tests and docs for this slice, committed and green.

## Dependencies
- CG-0MWZCM6I0005DYZ6

## Key Files
- `src/ui/scene-exit-presentation.ts`
- `tests/ui/scene-exit-presentation.browser.test.ts`

# Gym rendered precedent: Long Erasure wiring

**Summary:** Add a `sceneBanner` zone to the Gym Long Erasure layout (anchors from the GDD contract fixture) and wire the existing act-turn path (`GymLongErasureScene.applyChoice()`) to present the act transition through `presentSceneExit()`, replacing the current `TURN_CHANGE` + `announce()` pair.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json` gains a `sceneBanner` zone with anchors `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, `route` (geometry from `tests/fixtures/story-line/gdd-presentation-layout.json`), and `narrative`/`options` anchors are re-tuned so nothing collides.
2. The Gym layout contract test asserts the `sceneBanner` zone and all four anchors exist (`tests/gym/GymLongErasureLayout.test.ts`).
3. `GymLongErasureScene.applyChoice()` presents the act transition through `presentSceneExit()` — act title, the act's closing outcome word, and the route/beat ahead — replacing the current `TURN_CHANGE` + `announce()` pair.
4. The scene-title slot is optional (the spike has acts but no scenes): the banner shows the act title, closing outcome and route; the docs note that the scene-title slot fills once a game has scene-exit data.
5. `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts` asserts the act turn presents the banner (and skips it under reduced motion).
6. No absolute pixel coordinates are introduced; all positions come from SLL anchors.
7. **Covers parent AC 7.** Gym rendered precedent: `GymLongErasureScene`'s existing act-turn path (`applyChoice()`, where it currently plays `TURN_CHANGE` + `announce()`) presents the act transition through the helper, and `example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json` gains a `sceneBanner` zone using the anchors already pinned by the GDD contract fixture (`tests/fixtures/story-line/gdd-presentation-layout.json`: `actTitle`, `sceneTitle`, `outcome`, `route`), with the narrative/options anchors re-tuned so nothing collides. The Gym layout contract test asserts the zone and all four anchors exist; the Gym smoke profile stays green.

## Minimal Implementation
- Layout JSON update: add `sceneBanner` zone, re-tune `narrative`/`options` anchors.
- `GymLongErasureScene.ts`: import `presentSceneExit()`, replace the `TURN_CHANGE` + `announce()` block with a `presentSceneExit()` call.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureLayout.test.ts`: zone + anchor existence assertions.
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureScene.browser.test.ts`: banner presentation assertions.

# Exports, node-safe surface and documentation

**Summary:** Export the new helper and its types from the `@ui` barrel, add the module to `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts` **only if** the `check:ui-node-surface` gate proves it Phaser-free, and update all related documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `src/ui/index.ts` exports `planSceneExitPresentation`, `resolveSceneExitSfxKey`, `presentSceneExit`, and all associated types (`SceneExitPresentationOptions`, `SceneExitPlan`, `SceneExitStep`, `SceneExitPresentationHandle`).
2. Node-safe surface handled honestly: if the module is Phaser-free (Phaser as `import type` only), it is added to `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts`; if `npm run build`'s `check:ui-node-surface` gate proves it Phaser-bearing it is **not** added. Either way the gate and the build stay green.
3. `docs/ui-animations.md` gains a section beside `revealNarration`/`runSceneTransition`: helper signature, pacing row, reduced-motion path and SFX contract.
4. `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` Long Erasure entry gains a note on the `sceneBanner` presentation.

Either way the gate and the build stay green.

# Integration gate: full suite green and docs verified

**Summary:** Final verification slice — run the changed-scope and then full test suite, confirm the build's `check:ui-node-surface` gate is green, and verify the Gym smoke profile stays green with the new banner wiring.

6. **Covers parent AC 8.** Tests: Node unit tests for the planner, SFX selection, outcome channel and lifecycle idempotence (no Phaser), plus one browser test proving the banner renders, sequences its steps and completes instantly under reduced motion.
